title: Power Mean Extreme Cases: M_r → max/min
description: Formalizes lim_{r→+∞} M_r = max and lim_{r→-∞} M_r = min for two-variable power means. Sets up sandwich bounds and convergence framework.

meta.author: Classical analysis
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom (power mean monotonicity from parent). 5 sorries (rpow composition, limit theory).
originalContributions: Power mean definition for two variables
Sandwich bounds framework: min ≤ M_r ≤ max

overview.historicalContext: The power mean M_r converges to max and min as r → ±∞. This completes the chain from the parent file's monotonicity result.
overview.problemStatement: Prove lim_{r→+∞} M_r(a,b) = max(a,b) and lim_{r→-∞} M_r(a,b) = min(a,b).
overview.text: Sets up sandwich bounds and convergence framework. Technical rpow composition sorries remain.
overview.proofStrategy: Sandwich: min ≤ M_r ≤ max. As r → ∞, M_r = max·((1+(min/max)^r)/2)^(1/r) → max since (min/max)^r → 0.
keyInsights: The key is (b/a)^r → 0 for b < a and r → ∞
rpow composition ((x^r)^(1/r) = x) requires careful Mathlib handling

conclusion.summary: Framework for power mean extreme cases established. Technical rpow simplification sorries remain.
openQuestions: Prove rpow composition: (a^r)^(1/r) = a for a > 0, r ≠ 0
